Positive integer bases are consecutive. Intersecting with the interval of extreme positive bases drops only null measured fibers and preserves each retained fiber. Every real fiber in that interval has nonempty interior by Minkowski interpolation. The plane parametrization is an isometry on each tangential fiber; the mixed section weights carry no ambient slanted-plane Jacobian.

For d≥2, Brunn–Minkowski in dimension d−1 gives root concavity on the positive-section interval and hence adjacent log-concavity by AM–GM. For d=1, the positive sections are singletons of counting mass one and their projection is an interval. Either way the positive integer section weights have no gaps.

The minimum margin is convex in the base and the maximum margin concave, by interpolation of fiber minimizers and maximizers. Given a proper base z_0 and any distinct interior point of the section projection, extend the ray through it to a further section base. Strict signs at z_0 and weak signs at the further point give strict signs at the interior point. A supporting section can therefore occur only at an extreme real projection base, hence only at the first or last positive integer section weight. This includes real extremes at an integer and cases where an extreme cut is proper or section-null.

Disjoint and section-null cuts contribute zero. Since the left derivative is ≤0 and the right derivative ≥0, one convex combination is zero. Finite attainment and positive depth at an own-interior mark give a nonempty set of maximizing bases; separation by at least two is ruled out.
